newsitem.title: UK: Italian shares end down as Wall Street falls again.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end down as Wall Street falls again.

text.p: Milan stocks tumbled to a lower close reflecting losses in the domestic BTP bond market, an early fall on Wall Street and worries over the continued strength in the value of the dollar, dealers said.

Most blue chip stocks were marked down early with Olivetti off 1.87 percent at 629 lire after the company said it would get less than expected for its PC business from Piedmont, and Pirelli was down 2.02 percent at 4,750 lire despite its cables division winning a contract in Indonesia.
The blue-chip Mib30 index ended off 1.82 percent at 21,863 and the all-share Mibtel down 1.75 percent at 14,438.

Olivetti revised down the financial benefit gained from the sale of its PC division to Piedmont to 190 billion lire from 250 billion. The revision took into account of a "temporary" extension of Olivetti's holding in Piedmont, currently 19.7 percent against a stake of 12 percent after the sale in April.

Pirelli's cables division on Monday announced that it had won a contract as part of a consortium to build a new submarine power system linking the islands of Java and Bali in Indonesia worth in total $40 million.
Mobile phone group TIM was one of few shares to gain, up 1.27 percent at 6,150 lire, as scattered buyers emerged.
Other blue chips ended down with oil giant ENI off 1.72 percent at 10,300 lire, Fiat 0.27 percent easier at 5,925 lire, and food group Parmalat 0.95 percent lower at 2,515 lire.
